name: Gisborne
note: City: the regional hub and only large town on the East Coast, the base for the whole region (a destination in its own right, listed so the run can judge it).

name: East Cape
note: Coastal region (a destination area): the whole cape north of Gisborne, reached by State Highway 35, listed so the run can judge it.

name: Wairoa
note: Town (Hawke's Bay Regional Council area, DOC East Coast region): gateway to Lake Waikaremoana, Te Urewera and the Mahia Peninsula, listed for the run to place.

name: Gisborne City Vintage Railway
note: Heritage railway: a vintage rail line in Gisborne (Wikipedia and OSM only; no visitor guide among the sources read).

name: Tairāwhiti Museum
note: Museum: Māori taonga and local history, a surfing and ocean exhibit with the Star of Canada wheelhouse, in Gisborne.

name: Eastwoodhill Arboretum
note: Arboretum and garden: New Zealand's largest planting of North American trees, 35 km north-west of Gisborne, with walks, lovely in autumn.

name: Hackfalls Arboretum
note: Arboretum and gardens near Te Karaka, inland from Gisborne (named in Wikipedia's protected areas list only).

name: Gisborne Botanical Gardens
note: Public botanical gardens in the city (Wikipedia and OSM only; no visitor guide among the sources read).

name: Puhi Kai Iti / Cook Landing Site
wiki: Puhi Kai Iti / Cook Landing Site
note: Historic reserve: the Cook Landing Site and monument, where Captain Cook first landed in New Zealand in 1769 (DOC National Historic Reserve).

name: Titirangi
note: Hill reserve above the city: a Cook monument and a pōhutukawa planted by Diana, Princess of Wales, with views over the city.

name: Kaiti Hill
note: Hill and lookout over Gisborne, with a view of the city at sunrise. Named only in a Wikivoyage photo caption and the tourism sunrise guidance. Its Wikipedia name redirects to Titirangi (hill), a different hill, so it has no article of its own.

name: Gisborne Olympic Pool Complex
note: Pool complex: 50 m year-round lap pool, outdoor diving pools, zero-depth pool and summer hydro-slide, opposite Midway Beach (permanent venue, public pool).

name: Waikanae Beach
note: Beach: swimming and surf beach near the middle of Gisborne, running on into Midway Beach. (The scorer matched a Kapiti Coast spot of the same name; that is a different beach, so no existing match is recorded.)

name: Midway Beach
note: Beach: the continuation of Waikanae Beach, beside the Olympic Pool Complex.

name: Wainui Beach
note: Surf beach 7 km north of Gisborne, with the Wainui Store (fish and chips) and access to the coast north.

name: Makorori
note: Beach and surf area north of Gisborne (Wikivoyage spells it Makarori; named as one of the bays to visit beyond the city). No Wikipedia article.

name: Rere Rock Slide
note: Natural rock slide: a stream flows over a sloping rock into a pool, slid on body boards or tyres (a swimming-hole and waterslide). Its Wikipedia name redirects to the village of Rere, so the views are the village's and count as 0.

name: Tatapouri Reef
coordinates_source: OpenStreetMap, approximate (Tatapouri Fishing Club, the reef access point)
note: Reef: the Tatapouri reef walk on SH35, where guided ecology tours walk out to meet stingrays (tide-dependent; the reef is the place, the tour the means).

name: Gisborne RailBike Adventures
note: Operator: rail-bike rides on the old railway line out of Gisborne (the tourism board lists the operator; the line is the attraction, not a named place).

name: Gisborne Cycle Tour Company
note: Operator: one-day wine-tasting cycle tours, city tours and multi-day tours (a company, not a place).

name: Motu Outdoor Adventures
note: Operator: outdoor and river adventures (rafting on the Motū River) out of Gisborne (an operator, not a place).

name: Gisborne Wine Centre
note: Tasting room: local wine tastings and snack platters at Shed 3, the Inner Harbour (a venue, the wineries are the draw).

name: Gisborne wine region
note: Wine region: one of New Zealand's largest grape-growing regions around Gisborne, with vineyard and winery tours (an area, visited through its cellar doors).

name: Gisborne Farmers Market
note: Market: runs only on Saturday mornings (9:00-13:00), so a weekly market rather than a permanent venue.

name: Rhythm & Vines
note: Festival: a three-day music festival held in a vineyard at New Year (an annual event, not a permanent spot).

name: Wine & Food Gisborne
note: Festival: the annual Gisborne wine and food event held each October (an annual event, not a permanent spot).

name: Young Nick's Head
note: Headland: the first land sighted by Cook's expedition in 1769, a headland outside Gisborne with a historic monument.

name: Poverty Bay
note: Bay: the bay Gisborne sits on, named by Cook (a region-scale bay, its beaches and city are the visit).

name: Mōrere Springs Scenic Reserve
note: Scenic reserve with the Nga Hua o Mōrere hot springs at its entrance, coastal native forest and nīkau palms, on SH2 between Gisborne and Wairoa.

name: Mangakawa Track
note: Walking track in Mōrere Springs Scenic Reserve (DOC track).

name: Nikau Loop Track
note: Walking track in Mōrere Springs Scenic Reserve, through nīkau palms (DOC track).

name: Ridge Track (Mōrere)
note: Walking track in Mōrere Springs Scenic Reserve along the ridge (DOC track).

name: Te Tapuwae o Rongokako Marine Reserve
note: Marine reserve: 2,452 ha of reef and rocky shore north-east of Gisborne, for snorkelling and marine life (DOC; access subject to sea conditions). No Wikipedia article was found; coordinates to be taken from DOC.

name: Grays Bush Scenic Reserve Walks
note: Walks: bush walks through native forest near Gisborne (DOC).

name: Okitu Scenic Reserve Walk
note: Walk: a scenic reserve walk near Gisborne (DOC).

name: Otoko Walkway
note: Walkway at Otoko, on the coast near Gisborne (DOC).

name: Te Kuri Farm Walkway
note: Walkway on a working farm near Gisborne (DOC).

name: Marawaiwai Track
note: Track in Marawaiwai Scenic Reserve (DOC).

name: Whinray Scenic Reserve Track
note: Track in Whinray and Motu Scenic Reserves (DOC).

name: Waioeka Gorge Scenic Reserve
note: Scenic reserve: the Waioeka Gorge on SH2 between Gisborne and Ōpōtiki, with tracks such as Mangapumarumaru and Tauranga Loop (DOC).

name: Mount Hikurangi
note: Peak and tramp: Te Ara ki Hikurangi, the mountain climbed through Raukūmara Conservation Park (DOC names it as a climb).

name: Raukūmara Conservation Park
note: Conservation park: 115,000 ha of remote bush, with Mount Hikurangi, the Mōtū River rafting and Otipi Road biking (DOC).

name: Otipi Road Trail
note: Mountain-bike and walking trail on Otipi Road in Raukūmara Conservation Park (DOC names it as a highlight).

name: Mōtū River
note: River: rafting on the Mōtū River through Raukūmara Conservation Park (DOC names it; the river is a trip, not a single site). No Wikipedia article was found.

name: Mōtū
note: Settlement: the township at the gateway to Raukūmara Conservation Park, reached from Matawai (a base, not a sight).

name: Matawai
note: Settlement: a small inland township on SH2 with outdoor and wilderness activities (Wikivoyage names it as a town). The Wikipedia name matches the article Mātāwai.

name: Tolaga Bay
note: Settlement and bay: a small coastal township popular with holidaymakers, the base for Cooks Cove and the wharf (Wikivoyage, DOC).

name: Tolaga Bay Wharf
note: Wharf: a long concrete wharf at Tolaga Bay, named by Wikivoyage as the longest wharf in New Zealand.

name: Cooks Cove Walkway
note: Walkway to Cooks Cove, where Cook's Endeavour anchored and his crew fished in 1769 (DOC).

name: Tokomaru Bay
note: Settlement: a small bay township on SH35 between Tolaga Bay and Ruatoria (Wikivoyage names it as a place on the coast).

name: Anaura Bay
coordinates_source: OpenStreetMap (natural=bay, Wikipedia link); the bay centroid, the campsite and beach are the visit
note: Bay: a beach and DOC campsite reached off SH35 north of Tolaga Bay, where Cook landed to take on water in 1769.

name: Anaura Bay Walkway
note: Walkway: up to panoramic views over Anaura Bay from the scenic reserve (DOC).

name: Ruatoria
note: Town: the second largest town in the East Coast district, the main service centre of the Ruatoria side of East Cape.

name: Tikitiki
note: Village: the most easterly point of the New Zealand Highway network, on the Ruatoria road.

name: St Mary's Church, Tikitiki
note: Church: the Māori Anglican church at Tikitiki, a war memorial church (Wikipedia and OSM only; the public-access question is not settled by these sources).

name: Te Araroa
note: Town: a small beachside settlement famous for manuka honey, the base for the East Cape lighthouse and the Te Araroa trail.

name: East Cape Lighthouse
note: Lighthouse: on the easternmost point of the New Zealand mainland, 20 km along East Cape Road from Te Araroa (Wikivoyage: head there to see it).

name: Te Araroa Trail
note: Long-distance trail: the ~3,000 km walk from Cape Reinga to Bluff; its East Cape and Gisborne sections are in this region (a trail counted as one spot, sections judged on their own).

name: Hicks Bay
note: Settlement: a bay village on the East Cape road, north of Te Araroa (Wikivoyage lists it as a place on the cape).

name: Whangaparaoa
note: Settlement: the easternmost settlement in the Bay of Plenty on the East Cape road (Wikivoyage). Its Wikipedia name redirects to Whangaparāoa Peninsula in Auckland, so it is not the same place and has no article of its own.

name: Te Kaha
note: Settlement: a small community 65 km north-east of Ōpōtiki, a fishing and holiday base (Wikivoyage).

name: Waihau Bay
note: Settlement and bay: known for sports fishing and the setting for the film Boy (Wikivoyage).

name: Whanarua Bay
note: Bay: a holiday bay with accommodation near the East Cape highway (Wikivoyage names it with Maraehako Bay).

name: Maraehako Bay
note: Bay: a neighbouring holiday bay to Whanarua, popular with summer holidaymakers (Wikivoyage).

name: Raukokore Church
note: Church: a picturesque Anglican church standing isolated near the shore of Papatea Bay (Wikivoyage names it; a church, interior access not confirmed).

name: Papatea Bay
note: Bay: the bay at Raukokore on the East Cape coast (named by Wikivoyage as the setting for the church).

name: Whangara
note: Settlement and beach: the setting of the film Whale Rider, named by Wikivoyage for the film location (the film is a regional mention, not a stop).

name: Maraenui Hill Lookout
note: Lookout: a hill lookout named at the top of the East Cape Wikivoyage page (a viewpoint, the view is the stop).

name: Waipiro Bay
note: Settlement: a small bay settlement on the East Cape coast (Wikipedia only; no visitor guide among the sources read).

name: Te Puia Springs
note: Hot springs village inland from Gisborne (Wikipedia only; a hot-springs venue, which the visitor sources read did not describe).

name: Te Urewera National Park
note: National park: the home of Tūhoe, with lakes, forest and tracks, between the Bay of Plenty and Hawke's Bay (DOC; managed by Te Uru Taumatua).

name: Lake Waikaremoana
note: Lake: the large lake at the heart of Te Urewera, reached from SH38 (DOC names it; lake and shore walks).

name: Lake Waikaremoana Great Walk
note: Great Walk: a 46 km, 3-4 day tramp around Lake Waikaremoana (DOC Great Walk, bookings open for 2026/27).

name: Lake Waikareiti
note: Lake: an island-holding lake reached by the Waikareiti track from Lake Waikaremoana (DOC names the lake walk).

name: Lake Waikareiti Walk
note: Track: the walk to Lake Waikareiti from Lake Waikaremoana (DOC track).

name: Manuoha to Waikareiti Track
note: Track: a route through Te Urewera to Lake Waikareiti (DOC track).

name: Panekire Bluffs
note: Viewpoint: bluffs with incredible views over Lake Waikaremoana, a Great Walk highlight (DOC).

name: Korokoro Falls
note: Waterfall: on the Lake Waikaremoana Great Walk, which DOC calls well worth the detour.

name: Lake Kaitawa Fairy Springs Track
note: Track: a short walk to the Fairy Springs near Lake Kaitawa in Te Urewera (DOC track).

name: Ruapani Circuit Track
note: Track: a circuit walk in Te Urewera (DOC track).

name: Old Māori Trail
note: Track: an historic route through Te Urewera (DOC track).

name: Ngamoko Track
note: Track in Te Urewera (DOC track).

name: Ngutuoha Nature Trail
note: Nature trail in Te Urewera (DOC track).

name: Waimana Valley Tramping Tracks
note: Tramping tracks in the Waimana Valley, Te Urewera (DOC).

name: Lake Waikaremoana Area Short Walks
note: Short walks around Lake Waikaremoana (DOC group of short walks).

name: Te Urewera Visitor Centre (Te Kura Whenua)
note: Visitor centre: the Te Urewera visitor centre at Te Kura Whenua on SH38 by the lake (DOC names it; a visitor facility).

name: Waikaremoana Holiday Park
note: Holiday park: the lakeside holiday park by Te Urewera Visitor Centre (accommodation, an operator).

name: Tuai
note: Settlement: the village at the south end of Lake Waikaremoana (Wikipedia; a base near the lake).

name: Whirinaki Te Pua-a-Tāne Conservation Park
note: Conservation park: native forest with tracks and huts, on the border of Bay of Plenty and Hawke's Bay (DOC).

name: Whirinaki Waterfall Loop Track
note: Loop track to a waterfall in Whirinaki Te Pua-a-Tāne Conservation Park (DOC track).

name: Te Pua-a-Tāne Circuit
note: Circuit track through Whirinaki Te Pua-a-Tāne Conservation Park (DOC track).

name: Mahia Peninsula
note: Peninsula: the Māhia Peninsula between Wairoa and Gisborne, with beaches, the Portland Island lighthouse and scenic reserves (DOC names its track).

name: Mahia Peninsula Scenic Reserve Track
note: Track in the Māhia Peninsula scenic reserve (DOC track).

name: Te Reinga Scenic Reserve Walk
note: Walk in a Wairoa-area scenic reserve (DOC).

name: Waiatai Scenic Reserve Walk
note: Walk in a Wairoa-area scenic reserve (DOC).

name: Mangaone Caves Track
note: Track to the Mangaone caves near Wairoa (DOC).

name: Wairoa Museum
note: Museum: local history museum from early European-Māori contact to the present, on Marine Parade (free entry, donations welcome).

name: Old Portland Island Lighthouse
note: Lighthouse: a lighthouse moved from Portland Island to Wairoa, beside the bridge on Marine Parade.

name: Gaiety Theatre
note: Cinema: a restored theatre on Marine Parade showing films (a venue, the cinema is the visit). No single Wikipedia article.

name: Wairoa Riverside Walkway
note: Walkway: a 7.7 km riverside walk and cycleway from the lighthouse to Whakamahia Beach along the Wairoa River (Wikivoyage).

name: Sir James Carroll Walkway
note: Walkway: a 30-minute walk along the north bank of the Wairoa River opposite the town centre (Wikivoyage).

name: Wairoa Marine Parade
note: Riverfront: the Marine Parade, where the river widens into a lagoon, with birdlife and the lighthouse and museum beside it (Wikivoyage).

name: Mōkau Falls
note: Waterfall in Wairoa District (Wikipedia category only; no visitor guide among the sources read).

name: Whakaki Lagoon
note: Wetland lagoon near Wairoa (Wikipedia only; a birdlife wetland).

name: SS Talune
note: Shipwreck off the Wairoa coast (Wikipedia and OSM only; a dive site rather than a visitor stop).

name: Akuaku
note: Settlement ruins on the East Cape coast (Wikipedia and OSM only; an historic site with no visitor guide among the sources read).

name: Harry Barker Reserve
note: Local reserve in Gisborne (Wikipedia and OSM only; no visitor guide names it).

name: Childers Road Reserve
note: Local reserve in Gisborne (Wikipedia and OSM only; no visitor guide names it).

name: Whakarua Park
note: Park near Ruatoria (Wikipedia and OSM only; a local park).

name: Mount Arowhana
note: Peak in the Raukūmara ranges (Wikipedia and OSM only; no visitor guide among the sources read).

name: Maungahaumia
note: Peak inland of the East Coast (Wikipedia and OSM only; no visitor guide among the sources read).
